title: Plan §10's literal grep checklist over-fires on legitimate contrastive prose; interpreted by intent, not letter
detail: The checklist items `grep -ri "nestjs|fastify|postgres|docker|turbo"` (expect 0 outside plan §0.0) and `grep -ri "appointment|dealership|technician" apps/ packages/ docs/ directives/` (expect 0) both fire on docs/directives that legitimately explain what was rejected and why (e.g. "no Docker, no turbo" in docs/09_running_it.md; "Scenario 01 pushed its own correctness guarantee (no two overlapping appointments) into..." in docs/adr/0001). None of the hits reintroduce the actual technology or business domain — they are all cross-references to ../service-appointment-scheduler/ or explanations of an omission. Treated as satisfying the checklist's intent (nothing actually uses NestJS/Postgres/Docker/Turbo; nothing reintroduces dealership/technician domain vocabulary as a modeled concept) rather than its literal zero-hits wording. Documented here rather than silently accepted.

title: A partial PATCH on Shift needs a merged-state guard beyond Zod -- InvalidShiftTimeRangeError, not a second validator
detail: createShiftSchema/updateShiftSchema's .refine(endMinute > startMinute) only sees the PATCH BODY, not the existing row -- a request patching only { endMinute: 100 } against an existing { startMinute: 600, endMinute: 900 } passes Zod's refine trivially (startMinute is undefined in the patch) but would merge into an invalid overnight range if written through unchecked. UpdateShiftHandler merges the patch with the existing row and checks endMinute > startMinute itself, throwing InvalidShiftTimeRangeError (422) if violated -- same domain-constraint class as FeasibilityGate (enforced on already-well-typed data), not a second input validator; directives/zod_validation.md's rule 4 governs REQUEST validation, not a check that needs the existing DB row to evaluate. Verified live against Postgres: PATCH {endMinute:100} on a {600,900} shift returns 422 INVALID_SHIFT_TIME_RANGE, not a silently corrupted row.

title: Cross-scenario audit rule: process/convention directives must be diffable against the sibling scenario and differ ONLY in fill-in slots; business/domain docs may differ freely
detail: User's rule, stated explicitly: documents that are business-specific may differ between scenarios, but shared process/coding-architecture/testing/convention documents must stay the same. Enforced this pass by literally diffing every shared file between service-appointment-scheduler and demand-driven-staff-scheduler rather than reading each in isolation -- which is what surfaced the drift a per-file read had missed twice: memory_sop.md had silently DROPPED two things (the 'observability' routing-table category, and the whole 'see .ai/memory for real examples / this is AI-collaboration evidence' paragraph); cqrs_pattern.md had dropped the 'Response DTOs are FLAT' placement rule; qa_standard.md told the reader to run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint` when this repo has the same `npm run check` script scenario 01's copy names; testing_standard.md still described layer 3 as 'apps/web, real SQLite file' and prescribed a Vitest `vi.fn()` mocking pattern while apps/scheduler-api/eslint.config.mjs cross-references this very file for the Jest `jest.Mocked<T>` pattern. Also normalized STYLE: my earlier 'Reconciled to the real two-app shape (Phase F...)' headers read as changelog entries; scenario 01's convention is a terse 3-5 line provenance note saying what was ported/trimmed and why. Changelog belongs in .ai/PROJECT_STATUS.md, not in a rule file. Rule going forward: `diff ../<other-scenario>/directives/<file> directives/<file>` is part of finishing any edit to a shared directive -- remaining diff lines should be only domain examples and commands.

title: apps/web had NO .prettierrc of its own (unlike apps/scheduler-api and packages/shared-kernel) -- running a root-level `npx prettier --write` on it reformats to prettier's bare defaults (double quotes, semicolons), silently breaking the app's established single-quote/no-semicolon style
detail: apps/web's existing files (api-client.ts, create-schedule-form.tsx) were hand-written in single-quote/no-semicolon style matching apps/scheduler-api's/packages/shared-kernel's .prettierrc, but apps/web itself had no .prettierrc and no `format`/`format:check` script in package.json -- so `npm run format` (turbo run format) at the root silently skips apps/web (no script = turbo no-ops it), and that missing config was never noticed because nobody had run a bare `npx prettier --write` against it before. Hit this while building Phase 3's UI screens: ran `npx prettier --write apps/web/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` from the repo root to tidy 27 new/changed files, and it reformatted EVERY file (including the three pre-existing ones) to double-quote+semicolon defaults because prettier found no config anywhere in apps/web's ancestor chain up to the repo root. Fixed by adding apps/web/.prettierrc with the same singleQuote/semi:false/trailingComma:all values as apps/scheduler-api's, then re-running prettier -- restores the original style and makes it enforceable going forward. Lesson: before running a repo-root prettier command against a package, check that package has its own .prettierrc (or inherits one) -- an unformatted-by-convention package is not the same as a package with no opinion, and `npx prettier` will happily impose its defaults on the latter.
context: apps/web/.prettierrc (new file), apps/web/package.json (still has no format/format:check script)

title: A Client Component's `useState(propValue)` does NOT re-sync when the parent Server Component re-renders with a new prop after router.refresh() -- only the FIRST mount's value is used; caught in roster-manager.tsx's 'Suggest from data' caption going stale after saving new parameters
detail: `RosterManager` seeded `const [currentSuggestedN, setCurrentSuggestedN] = useState(suggestedN)` from a server-fetched prop. After 'Save parameters' succeeded (PATCH 200, confirmed via network log) and called `router.refresh()`, the Server Component re-fetched a fresh `suggestedN.current` and passed it down as a new prop -- but React does NOT re-invoke `useState`'s initializer on a prop change to an already-mounted component, so the caption kept showing the OLD value ('this schedule currently uses N = 18') even though the schedule had just been saved with N=20. Fixed by NOT capturing the always-fresh half of that data (`current`, which is just `schedule.transactionsPerStaffHour`) into state at all -- read it directly from the `schedule` prop every render, which DOES update on `router.refresh()` since it's a fresh prop value each render, not a captured initial value. Only the half that genuinely needs an explicit user action to change (`suggested`, populated by clicking 'Suggest from data') stays as local state. General rule for this codebase's `router.refresh()`-based mutation pattern (`directives/frontend_standard.md` §2): a Client Component may hold local state for fields the USER edits (form inputs), but must read server-owned, non-input values directly from props every render, never mirror them into `useState(prop)` -- that mirror only initializes once and silently goes stale on every later refresh.

title: index.ts export list now grouped with per-stage comments (Stage 0..5) and a header note naming the 4 exports the app actually calls
detail: User found index.ts hard to read: a flat list of 8 export lines with no indication of which stage each line belonged to, or which exports were load-bearing for apps/scheduler-api versus only exposed for the package's own tests/validateRoster replay. Comment-only change, no logic touched: added a header note ("Only 4 of the exports below are what the app actually calls -- generateRoster, summarise, suggestTransactionsPerStaff, validateRoster") plus a one-line stage label above each re-export (Stage 0 shared arithmetic / Stage 1 demand-to-required / Stage 2 required-to-shift / Stage 3a gate+state / Stage 3b assignment passes / Stage 4 rebalance / Stage 5 diagnostics). Convention going forward: when index.ts gains a new re-export, tag it with its pipeline stage inline rather than leaving the list flat -- the stage number is what a reader actually needs to jump to the right file, not just the export name. Companion reference (not committed to repo, published as a Claude Artifact for the user) enumerates all 36 functions/methods package-wide as PUB (reachable via index.ts) / PKG (exported at file level but never re-exported through index.ts, e.g. utilisationOf/compareByNameThenId in assignment/utilisation.ts) / PRIV (no export keyword) -- confirms only 14 of 36 are public and only 4 of those are what the app calls.

title: build-scheduling-input.ts refactored from 4 positional args to an options object -- convention going forward: a shared row-shaping function with more than ~3 params takes an options object, not positional threading
detail: buildSchedulingInput(schedule, staff, shifts, demandCells) was already at 4 positional args before the stretch goals; H4 needed a 5th (unavailability) and roles needed a 6th/7th (staffRoles, shiftRoleRequirements) -- widened to a single BuildSchedulingInputOptions object instead of growing the positional list further, since call-site correctness for 6-7 positional args of the same param count/shapes (arrays of domain rows) is not something a type-checker catches if two are transposed. All 4 call sites (auto-schedule, add-assignment, get-coverage, suggest-n) updated to named-field object literals; optional fields (unavailability/staffRoles/shiftRoleRequirements) default to [] internally so pre-existing call sites that do not need H4/roles data (add-assignment, suggest-n) do not have to pass them. Rule: when a shared shaping/mapping function used across multiple handlers needs a new parameter, prefer widening an existing options-object signature (or converting to one at the 4th positional arg) over adding another positional slot -- the failure mode of a transposed same-typed positional arg is silent and type-checker-invisible.
